text:
Both teams arrive on the skids. The Flyers (PHI) open a five-game road trip after a 4-2 home loss to MIN on Tuesday, leaving them 1-3-1 in their last five and without Rasmus Ristolainen. The Rangers (NYR) finish a four-game home stand having just snapped a four-game winless run with a 3-1 win over STL, though they are 1-4-0 in their last five and still without Sean Durzi. Braden Schneider has taken on Durzi's minutes, up to 20:55 a night from 18:11.

The numbers favor New York. At five on five, NYR has taken 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in its games, PHI only 40%, and our model has the Rangers at 3.27 expected goals tonight to 2.79. PHI also takes 4.3 penalties a game, which keeps feeding opposing power plays. In net, Joseph Woll is the projected PHI starter and sits at +3.6 goals saved above expected (how many more goals he's stopped than an average goalie would on the same shots) this season, but was at -7.4 last year. Dylan Garand, projected for NYR, is at +1.4 this year and +3.9 over three games last season.

For the Flyers, Matvei Michkov has 11 points in his last ten games, and the chances behind them look real. Trevor Zegras, born in Bedford, plays near home and is at 28% to score in our numbers. Alexis Lafrenière and Pavel Dorofeyev are both at 32% for the Rangers. Dorofeyev is also our under-the-radar pick: a third-liner at about 16 minutes a night whose shots have been dangerous, at 4.5 expected goals over his last 10 games.
